question.text: Which of the following is NOT part of the 'Disclosures on Governance aspects' that an NPO must disclose on an annual basis (within 60 days from end of FY)?

answer.text: Category-wise amount of monies raised and utilised during the quarter.
Governance Structure (board and management committee, mandates, membership, charters, policies and internal controls).

explanation.text: The Logic: Governance aspects include ownership and legal form, governance structure, details of governing body, executives with key responsibilities, meeting frequencies and attendance, potential risks and mitigation, ethics advice mechanisms, remuneration policies, grievance redressal, and registration certificates. Category-wise utilisation is a QUARTERLY 91F statement, not a governance annual disclosure. The Trap: The trap swaps one correct (governance) item for a 91F quarterly utilisation line, relying on the candidate's familiarity with category-wise reporting as a 'NPO disclosure'. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/III-C governance disclosures for main-board boards cover similar ground; XXIII focuses on the 91(C) Governance list. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When the SIA sees a 91F-style utilisation line smuggled into the governance disclosure, treat it as a red-flag that the NPO is conflating regulatory buckets. Separate the governance pack from the utilisation pack explicitly in the management letter.
